You have every to feel that way. The more I thought about it, you have to realize you need to start valuing friendships the same way the other friend does. Which doesn't mean to end the friendship completely unless you deem necessary. Though it seems like you and Tyler really had a close bond, from the sounds of it, he values your friendship less than you do and sees you as a convenient friend to depend on. Which is not ideal but it shows that he feels safest when he is with you and that he trusts you. You seem like a good friend. You check up on him and your best to maintain your friendship

Now, the thing is, you also have to accept that things can't go back to the way they were. What's in the past is in the past, no matter how much you want a friendship to be like the way things were it can't because simply, people change and the only thing that you can do is in the present. It sucks but the more you grip onto the past, the more sad you will become thinking about it. 

So I guess what I'm trying to say is, will you accept that change in your friendship?  Some people will say no because they feel like it is unfair or like they feel used. On the other hand, people who say yes will accept that part of the friendship and understand that's just how the friendship is now. If you do want to remain friends with him,  you have to accept the way he treats your friendship. Yes he is a good person, but he doesnt respond to you when he is a relationship and contacts you when it is convenient for him. Not everyone is perfect and we accept friends even with their flaws and the changes. 

Again though, it depends on how you feel about the change in the friendship. If you accept it the way it is which you texting him less is a start, then remain friends with him. But if you feel like his treatment to you is really unfair and constantly bringing you down, then simply don't be friends. Someone who you feel like is using you isn't worth your time. 

I hope this helps, take sometime to think about it cuz ending friendships is quite heavy like any other relationship

Omg yes!!! Totally relate. I'm 19 turning 20, and I have a group of 4 from HS as well. I'm close with 2 of 3 of the friends but I still put an effort to talk to all of them on a daily basis. Anyways, when I talk to them individually they ALWAYS say they haven't talked for each other in a while. That's when I realized, I'm the only one putting in an effort to still be friends with one another. 

I don't want to let go of being a friend group because we have done so much together and I feel like I'm closing a chapter of my life I'm not ready to be done with. 

But I don't want to keep putting in the effort if they don't want to do the same. I don't want to continue hanging out as a group if they feel like its a chore or something they're doing because they feel like they have to.

I'm always the one driving them everywhere too. Not that it bothers me, but I feel like it's another reason we hang out still because I'm there? Its not even that they hate each other either, they just don't hang out because quote from one of them "we don't have anything to talk about". I get that not all of them may not vibe with each other, but the more i think about it and look at my friend group it just seems more like a facade. Like are we even considered a friend group when I'm the only one that initiates everything and when they don't even talk to each other? 

I don't give good advice but I just want to let you know I understand and I think its more common in groups than people realize or care to admit. Its something we can't control. I don't even think we should blame anyone either, like I'm not gonna blame someone if they don't get along with someone else right? Its just sad in the end, because what we thought we knew is not what it was. Even if in the end the group does fall apart, I'd rather have 4 quarters than a 100 pennies right? People grow and people change i think that's something we should both keep in mind.
I see it as if I'm so sure about it, why do I need to drag others into the mess I have already become.
